content:
Looking at each net: the row of four squares forms the side ring of the cube, and each pair of triangular flaps must join to cover exactly one half of the top face and one half of the bottom face each.

- **A:** Top flaps (on squares 2,3) fold into complementary halves of the top; bottom flaps likewise for the bottom. Works.
- **B:** Top flaps cover the top face halves; bottom flaps (on squares 1,4) meet along the other diagonal to complete the bottom. Works.
- **C:** Top flaps (on squares 1,4) form complementary halves of the top face, but the bottom flaps (on squares 1 and 4, pointing outward) fold onto the **same** half of the bottom face — they overlap, leaving the other half open. Fails.
- **D:** Top flaps (squares 1,3) and bottom flaps (squares 1,3) each form complementary diagonal halves. Works.
- **E:** Top flaps (squares 1,3) and bottom flaps (squares 2,4) each form complementary halves. Works.

Only net C leaves a gap (with overlapping triangles) when folded.
